claims.claim: William Horrocks of Stockport patented an improved power-loom in 1802 featuring better cloth take-up.
claims.episode_span: Horrocks’s 1802 and 1813 patents added a reliable take-up motion
claims.supporting_quote: 1802 William Horrocks, a Stockport cotton manufacturer, patented an improved power-loom. It featured a more effective way of winding the woven cloth onto a beam at the back of the loom

claims.claim: Richard Roberts patented a cast-iron power loom in 1822; the 1830 version featured robust cast-iron frames.
claims.episode_span: Roberts took the next step in his 1822 patent and the 1830 production version by casting the entire side frames as single iron pieces.
claims.supporting_quote: The Roberts loom was a cast-iron power loom introduced by Richard Roberts in 1830. It was the first loom that was more viable than a hand loom and was easily adjustable and reliable

claims.claim: In 1823 a steam-loom weaver could weave 7 pieces; in 1826, 12 to 15 pieces, while a hand-loom weaver produced 2 pieces per week in 1814.
claims.episode_span: Weekly output per weaver rose from two pieces to twelve or fifteen
claims.supporting_quote: In 1823, a steam-loom weaver could weave 7 pieces; in 1826, 12 to 15 pieces

claims.claim: UK power looms rose from 14,150 in 1820 to approximately 100,000 by 1833.
claims.episode_span: By 1833 Britain had roughly 100,000 power looms
